title: 8-round AES-192: Unrefined early-abort candidate stage

target.description: Reduced 8-round AES-192 with whitening k_-1, final MixColumns omitted, and u_i=MC^-1(k_i). Pair-filtering stage returns candidate subkeys; it stops before multiset membership and complete recovery.

setting.key_relation: One fixed standard AES schedule; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: General fixed key; no weak-key subset is specified.
setting.plaintext_model: 2^113 chosen plaintexts yield approximately2^144 pairs to examine.
assumptions: The four-round one-byte differential is modeled at2^-120; Observation5 enumerates middle states using an average S-box count.
Wrong-key multisets are modeled random. The journal's separate probability proof has documented count/max-probability issues.
Reported time is the online stage; preprocessing is explicit and key-independent. Partial-encryption conversion factors are author estimates.

success.description: True AES192 k7/u6/whitening tuple retained in the complete unrefined PhaseA candidate lists within named model M_pair. This is candidate retention, not unique subkey identification or full-master-key recovery. M_pair assumes that the JOINT right-pair indicators on the fixed true-key delta-set partition have the law induced by a uniform permutation on \(N=2^{128}\) states. This joint extension is stronger than the source marginal random-permutation approximation of Section4.2/footnote5; it is an explicit heuristic premise, not an actual-AES theorem. No assertion that every AES output or wrong-key multiset is uniformly random is made. The existing \(2^{81}\) disjoint structures of \(2^{32}\) plaintexts partition, after the true round0, into \(S=2^{105}\) disjoint delta-sets of \(q=256\) states. This is only an analytical partition of the same \(2^{113}\) already queried blocks. Let X count within-set pairs agreeing in the15 inactive output bytes. Exactly \(e=Sq(q-1)/2\) edges are tested; \(a=Sq(q-1)(q-2)\) ordered distinct-edge pairs share a vertex. Define \(p=(q-1)/(N-1)\), \(p_A=(q-1)(q-2)/((N-1)(N-2))\), and \(p_D=p(N(q-1)-4q+6)/((N-2)(N-3))\). Then \(\mu=ep\) and \(\nu=ap_A+(e(e-1)-a)p_D\) are the exact first and second factorial moments. The pointwise Bonferroni inequality gives \(\Pr_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}}[X>0]\ge\max\{0,\mu-\nu/2\}>49/100\), verified by exact integer arithmetic. This accounts for shared plaintexts and sampling without replacement, with no independent-pair or Poisson assumption and no conversion of expected one into63%. If X is positive, native exhaustive per-column lookup and aggregation include the actual tuple, and exact key-schedule identities retain it. Therefore the bound concerns the stated candidate-list output. Complete untruncated enumeration is required; estimated list lengths and the source work conversion do not certify a hard runtime cap. No multiset-table or Observation5 cardinality bound, wrong-key rejection, extra data/repetition, late-stage filtering or remaining-master-key search enters this event. Original native time/data/setup units, candidate counts and source conflicts remain unchanged. Earlier unquantified acquisition statements remain historical source observations; this is only a subsequent derived conditional model bound.

review.scope: Verified the explicit M_pair implication: native query partition, exact shared/disjoint-edge moments under the stated joint finite-permutation indicator law, Bonferroni inequality, rational49/100 lower bound and retention by complete unrefined PhaseA. This does not prove the joint law for concrete AES, unique or full-key recovery, a fixed runtime, source cost calibration, Observation5 or candidate-list concentration.

components.description: Section4.2 / footnote5 models the original inner four-round one-byte-in/one-byte-out differential at about2^-120 under a random-permutation approximation. This is per eligible pair, not probability of finding a pair, table inclusion, or key recovery.

Sections4.3/6: actual AES192 round-key bytes satisfy the16-bit u6-to-k7 consistency and8-bit whitening-to-k7 identity. This is true-key retention by schedule consistency, conditional on the correct pair/hypothesis, not an independent random-key acceptance or a complete recovery guarantee.

Section6 basic PhaseA: given an examined pair satisfying the original four-round inner differential under the true AES192 key, exhaustive column lookup includes its actual intermediate values, aggregation includes the actual k7/u6/whitening tuple, and true key-schedule identities do not discard it. The complete per-pair candidate list therefore contains the true tuple. This extends the existing schedule-only retention event to the whole unrefined PhaseA lookup/filter procedure. Condition on complete enumeration, with no list truncation or hard runtime cutoff. Finding a right pair among the native2^144 examined pairs at2^113 chosen plaintexts is not quantified; the estimated2^24 output count is not a worst-case bound. No multiset-table coverage assumption is needed for this PhaseA-only event. This is conditional candidate retention, not whole-stage success or unique/full-key recovery.
